data.content_ref: inline:The target fails to identify the single mechanism that best explains cross-city variance in the nocturnal UHI gap. It attributes the variance primarily to 'the total volume of masonry and asphalt relative to city size,' but the most well-supported single mechanism in urban climatology is the urban sky view factor (SVF) — the obstruction of the view to the sky by buildings, which traps longwave radiation and suppresses radiative cooling. The target mentions thermal mass and impervious area as the main modulators, which are secondary; by centering the cross-city explanation on stored energy volume rather than radiative geometry, it does not answer the second half of the problem correctly.
